textbookText: 16. Though males have both X and Y sex chromosomes, some of them have only male or only female kids. Why?
Ans:- Some males have only male or only female children due to chance, not because they produce one type of sperm. Male
sperms carry either X or Y chromosomes, and which one fertilizes the egg determines the sex of the child.
17. Meiosis cell division is also called reductional cell division. Why?
Ans:- Meiosis is called reductional division because it reduces the number of chromosomes to half in gametes, ensuring that
the chromosome number remains constant after fertilization.
18. Mitosis cell division is also called equational cells division. Why?
Ans:- Mitosis is called equational division because the number of chromosomes remains equal in the daughter cells as in the
parent cell.
19. Meiosis cell division brings variation. Why?
Ans:- Meiosis brings variation because of crossing over and independent assortment of chromosomes during gamete
formation, which produces new genetic combinations.
20. What is a chromosome? Clarify the role of chromosomes in the body of living beings.
Ans:- A chromosome is a thread-like structure made up of DNA and protein found in the nucleus. It carries genes that control
the heredity, growth, and development of living beings.
21. Explain the importance of mitosis cell division in the growth and development of the body.
Ans:- Mitosis is important for growth and development because it helps in increasing the number of cells, repairing damaged
tissues, and maintaining genetic stability in body cells.
22. Clearly explain the role of genes in the transmission of hereditary characteristics in organisms.
Ans:- Genes are units of heredity located on chromosomes. They control the transmission of hereditary characteristics from
parents to offspring by carrying genetic codes in the DNA.
23. A couple gave birth to 3 sons. Does it mean that the testes of the male-produced sperms have Y-chromosomes only?
Clarify it.
Ans:- The birth of three sons does not mean the father produces only Y-carrying sperms. Males produce both X and Y
sperms, and the sex of the child depends on which sperm fertilizes the egg by chance.

29. When tall pea plants and dwarf pea plants are cross pollinated, tall plants are produced in the first filial generation. Why?
Ans:- When tall and dwarf pea plants are cross-pollinated, only tall plants appear in the F₁ generation because tallness is a
dominant character and masks the dwarf trait.
30. When seff-breeding is done between hybrids, different types of offspring are produced. Why?
Ans:- When self-breeding is done between hybrids, different types of offspring are produced because of segregation and
recombination of genes during meiosis, which creates genetic variation.
